info.description: Reference documentation for the PwnForge API.

get.summary:
Public, unauthenticated. Returns every currently active alert, highest
priority first.
get.description: An empty array when no alert is active.

post.description:
Takes the handle returned alongside an `email_not_verified` failure, or
the token of an earlier verification link, not an email address: the
caller has already proven it holds the password or the mailbox. The new
link goes to the address on file.

422.description: validation_failed, invalid_body or token_invalid

post.summary: Marks an email address as verified.
post.description:
POST rather than GET: mail clients and spam scanners prefetch links, and a
GET would let them burn the token before the user clicks. The frontend
page reads the token from the URL and posts it.

Always answers 202, whether or not the address belongs to an account:
a different answer would turn this route into a way to test which
addresses are registered.

post.summary: Rotates the session and issues a fresh access token.
post.description:
Consumes the `refresh_token` cookie and replaces it. The presented token
is revoked on every rotation, and presenting it again is treated as a
replay: the whole session chain is then revoked.

post.summary: Creates an account without opening a session, or does nothing visible.
post.description:
Answers 202 with no body and no cookie, the same whether the address was
free, held by a verified account or held by a registration nobody
confirmed: registration never says whether an address has an account
(see `auth_service::register`). The address gets the mail: the
verification link of the new account, or a notice to its holder.

202.description: Accepted, with no body: the same answer whether the address was free or already had an account

AccentColor.description:
The accent colour of a team or a workspace: one closed palette shared by
both. Any other value, a hex code included, is refused with 422
`invalid_body`.

CancelReason.description: Why a cancelled invitation was cancelled.

expires_at.description:
Seven days from now when left out, at most thirty
(`invitation_expiry_too_far` beyond).

invited_email.description:
Invites whoever holds this address: an account with it verified sees
the invitation among its pending ones and accepts it there, or by the
link the mail carries; anyone else can create an account with it
first. Nothing is joined without that step.

Mutually exclusive with `username`. The answer is the same whether an
account holds the address or not: it is matched when the invitee
reads their invitations, never here.

max_uses.description: Ignored, and set to 1, when `username` or `invited_email` is given.

username.description:
The only account allowed to accept, by username. Left out for a
generic invitation link, which anyone holding the token may accept.
Mutually exclusive with `invited_email`.

CreateWorkspaceInput.description:
Payload for POST /workspaces. A solo workspace always belongs to the
caller.

color.description: The palette shared with teams, see `AccentColor`.

CreateWorkspaceInvitationRequest.description:
Payload for POST /workspaces/{slug}/invitations. The expiry is not the
author's to choose: every workspace invitation lasts seven days.

invited_email.description:
The address invited. The answer is the same whether an account holds
it or not; an account that has it verified sees the invitation among
its pending ones.

username.description:
The account invited, by username. Same bounds as
`CreateInvitationRequest::username`.

CreatedTeamInvitation.description: A generic link with its token (TeamLinkResponse), or a targeted invitation without one (TeamInvitationResponse)

EffectiveMember.description:
One person with access to a workspace, with the role that applies there
once team inheritance and workspace overrides are resolved. Excluded
members are not listed.

invited_by.description:
For a guest, the author of the invitation they accepted; `null` for
everyone else, and once the author's account is gone.

joined_at.description:
When this person gained access to *this workspace*, which is not the
same date as joining the team: a guest's admission to the workspace, a
team member's arrival in the team, and a solo owner's creation of the
workspace.

EmailConfigResponse.description:
What the backend read from its environment, so the operator can check that
the .env is what the process actually understood. Never carries the SMTP
password nor the API key: a wizard is not a reason to expose secrets.

smtp_auth.description: Whether credentials are configured, not what they are.

EmailNotVerifiedErrorResponse.description:
`email_not_verified`, carrying the token needed to request a new
verification mail without a second round trip.

GuestRole.description: The role a workspace invitation grants: a guest holds at most `member`.

HealthResponse.description:
Reported as strings rather than booleans: a monitoring probe reads the
same shape whether it looks at the top-level status or a single component.

status.description: "ok" when every component is reachable, "down" otherwise.

InvitationStatus.description:
Where an invitation stands. `expired` is also what a pending one past its
date reads as, before the cleanup records it.

InvitationTarget.description: Whom an invitation names, as the invitation lists show it.

InvitationTokenRequest.description:
An invitation token, in the body so it stays out of the request span and
the access logs, as `JoinTeamRequest` does.

LegalAcceptanceInput.description:
Versions the client says it displayed. Embedded in `RegisterRequest` and
used as the body of `POST /api/v1/legal/accept`.

The client sends what it showed rather than a bare boolean, so that a tab
left open for three weeks cannot silently accept a superseded text.

LegalStatusDto.description: Where the user stands with respect to the current documents.

accepted_terms_version.description: Versions currently on record, `null` if never accepted.

effective_at.description:
RFC 3339, present only while a revision is published but not yet
enforced.

LegalVersionStaleErrorResponse.description:
`legal_version_stale`, carrying the current versions so the client can
re-prompt immediately.

LegalVersionsDto.description:
Versions in force, served unauthenticated so the registration form can
send back what it displayed rather than a bare boolean.

PublicAlertResponse.description: An active alert, as every visitor sees it.

turnstile_site_key.description:
The Turnstile site key the protected forms render their widget with,
or `null` when the instance has Turnstile off.

SetMemberRoleRequest.description:
Payload for PATCH /workspaces/{slug}/members/{user_id}. `captain`, or any
value not listed, is refused at deserialization (422 `invalid_body`).

default_timezone.description:
IANA identifier, never a UTC offset: offsets change twice a year while
the identifier carries the whole rule.

SetupStatusResponse.description:
Answered without a token: the frontend needs it to decide whether to show
the wizard at all, before it has anything to authenticate with.

SimpleErrorResponse.description:
`{ "error": "invalid_credentials" }` and every other single-code failure.
Covers the majority of the error surface.

error.description: Stable machine-readable code, never a human sentence.

TeamInvitationPreview.description:
What the invitee sees before accepting by the link: enough for the
confirmation screen, and nothing about anyone else.

invited_by.description: The author, `null` once their account is gone.

invited_user_id.description:
The account named by username. `null` for an invitation by address,
whether or not an account holds it.

TeamLinkResponse.description:
The answer to the creation of a generic link: the invitation and the
token its link carries. The only answer that ever holds a token: a
targeted invitation's goes to its invitee's mail alone, and no listing
shows one.

invited_by.description:
The author of the invitation this member accepted, when they joined
by one. `null` for the team's creator, for members from before this
was recorded, and once the author's account is gone.

avatar_version.description:
`null` when the team has no avatar. Otherwise the cache-busting version
the client puts in the avatar URL, which it builds from the id:
`/api/v1/avatars/teams/{id}/{avatar_version}/256.webp`.

member_count.description: How many members the team has, its Captain included.

my_role.description:
Current user's role in this team, avoids an extra frontend round trip
to know which actions to show.

TeamRole.description: A member's role within a team.

TeamSummary.description:
A team as another resource names it: enough to show its name and
monogram, nothing about its members.

avatar_version.description:
Same contract as `TeamResponse.avatar_version`, and `null` as well
for a reader who is not on the team: the avatar is served to its
members only.

TransferCaptaincyRequest.description:
Names the member who becomes Captain. The current Captain becomes an
Admin in the same step.

UnprocessableErrorResponse.description:
The envelope of every 422. `fields` is present only when `error` is
`validation_failed`, mapping each offending field to the validator codes
it failed; every other 422 code (`invalid_body`, `invitation_expired`,
...) is a bare `{ "error": ... }`.

error.description: Stable machine-readable code, never a human sentence.

fields.description:
Field name to the list of validator codes it failed. Only with
`validation_failed`.

UpdateWorkspaceInput.description:
Payload for PATCH /workspaces/{slug}. The mode, the team and the owner
cannot be changed, and the avatar is changed through
POST /api/v1/avatars/workspaces/{id}.

description.description: Absent leaves it unchanged, null clears it, a string sets it.

ends_at.description: Same three states as `starts_at`, and must be after it.

name.description: Same bounds as `CreateWorkspaceInput.name`, checked only when present.

starts_at.description:
Absent leaves it unchanged, null clears it, a date sets it. Must be
before `ends_at`, the stored one when only this bound is sent.

UserResponse.description:
The account holding the session, as the auth routes return it: only ever
built from the caller's own row, never from another account.

avatar_version.description:
`null` when the account has no avatar. Same contract as
`TeamResponse.avatar_version`, under
`/api/v1/avatars/users/{id}/{avatar_version}/256.webp`.

ValidateAdminRequest.description: The administrator half of `SetupRequest`, checked on its own.

WorkspaceInvitationPreview.description:
What the invitee sees before accepting by the link: enough for the
confirmation screen, and nothing about anyone else.

WorkspaceInvitationResponse.description:
One workspace invitation, as its creation, the workspace's lists and the
invitee's own list show it. Never with its token: that goes to the
invitee's mail alone, and only its hash is stored.

accepted_by.description: Once accepted, the account that did.

invited_by.description: The author, `null` once their account is gone.

invited_email.description:
Only while the invitation is pending: the address is erased as soon
as it is accepted, declined, cancelled or expired.

invited_user_id.description:
The account named by username. `null` for an invitation by address,
whether or not an account holds it.

target.description: `username` or `email`: a workspace has no generic link.

WorkspaceResponse.description:
One workspace as GET, POST and PATCH return it, with the caller's own
access in `my_role`.

WorkspaceRole.description:
A role a member can be given on one workspace: every team role but
Captain, which belongs to the team and changes only by transfer. A guest
holds at most `member` (`guest_role_above_member` otherwise).

WorkspaceSummary.description: One workspace in the caller's list.

my_role.description:
The caller's access, resolved as every route resolves it: an override
set on this workspace wins over the team role.

oneOf.description:
The workspace's team, `null` for a solo workspace. A guest sees it
too, while the team's own routes stay closed to them.

WriteupVisibility.description: The visibility a new writeup of the workspace starts with.
